claim: For every integer \(n\ge 2\), let \(C_n\) be the \(2n\)-point crown with minimal points \(a_i\), maximal points \(b_i\), and strict relations \(a_i<b_i\) and \(a_i<b_{i-1}\), with indices in \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\). Let \(F_2(C_n)=\{(x,y)\in C_n\times C_n:x\ne y\}\) carry the induced product order. Then the first-coordinate projection \(\pi_1:F_2(C_n)\to C_n\) is a weak homotopy equivalence. Consequently \(F_2(C_n)\) has \(2n(2n-1)\) points, is a finite model of \(S^1\), and \(|\mathcal K(F_2(C_n))|\simeq S^1\).

integrity.finite_stress_test: verify.py reconstructs all crowns, deleted products, fibers, beat cores, and mod-two order-complex Betti vectors for 2<=n<=12.
integrity.proof_basis: Each minimal-open-set inverse image of the projection is explicitly reduced to one point by beat-point deletions, after which McCord's theorem applies.
integrity.unproved_limits: No statement is made for three or more points, unordered configurations, or arbitrary finite circle models.

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns ordered two-point configurations in the Alexandrov finite crown.
It does not cover unordered configurations, three or more particles, arbitrary finite models of the circle, or finite-space homotopy equivalence.
The finite checker samples parameters only; the universal quantifier is justified by the symbolic beat-point proof.
title: Two-point configurations of finite crowns retain the circle weak type
